pages.text: "Yum, gulp! Yum, gulp!" Moya grazed beside the waterhole. Nia the long-necked giraffe slowly chewed acacia leaves nearby. "Nia, hurry! Let's race to the rocky hill!"
Moya grabbed a huge mouthful and swallowed without chewing. Grab, gulp, grab, gulp! "The faster I eat, the sooner I play!" Their cheeks bulged. Nia was still chewing one bite.
Suddenly—"Ack! Ack!" Stiff dry grass stuck in Moya's throat. Shaking their neck didn't help. Tears rolled down their muzzle. Nia stretched their neck out in alarm.

Mom hurried over and gently stroked Moya's neck with her muzzle. "Slowly. A little sip of water." Moya drank, and the grass slipped down. "You swallowed too quickly. Shall we learn to eat slowly?" Moya nodded.
Mom told a story. "Your teeth are flat stones. The upper and lower stones grind stiff grass soft." Moya imagined it. Rub, rub—soft grass! "That's why I need to chew well!"
"Let's try like Nia. A little bite, lots of chewing, then swallow!" Mom whispered. Nia said shyly, "I chew twenty times... Want to see who chews longer?" Moya looked up.
Moya took a little bite. Chew, chew, chew! One, two, three... Sweet juice came out of the grass. "Was it always this sweet?" Chew well, take your time!
After a slow meal, Moya's throat felt clear and their tummy comfortable. Not one cough! "Nothing gets stuck when I eat slowly!" Moya whinnied. Nia smiled as they chewed.
Now Moya knew the steps. "One, a little bite! Two, chew lots of times! Three, swallow when it's all chewed!" The next day, Moya took small bites again. Chew well, take your time!
Mom nuzzled Moya's cheek. "What a fine zebra who chews well!" Slow chewing made the grass tastier and Moya's throat comfortable. "Nia, now let's race!"
